answer: Running 267 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the dawn schedule in the grove ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the nectar checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 19 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
